items.title: Oracle Has the Biggest Upside of Any Megacap Right Now: 54%
items.summary: Oracle's cloud business is growing faster than it has in years, yet the stock has been cut nearly in half. Our model finds a jarring disconnect between what the business is doing and what the market is pricing in.

items.title: Why Is Everyone Ignoring Snap Stock's High Cash Yield?
items.summary: Snap (SNAP) stock is 58% below its two-year high. At that price, Snap's free cash flow equals 8.1% of its market value, against 4.5% for the median S&P 500 company. With Snap's debt counted, that cash yield is 6.2%. A yield that high means a business on sale, or one the market expects to shrink. So why are investors paying so little for Snap's cash.

items.title: How Has Microsoft's Story Changed In A Year?
items.summary: Microsoft's management stressed Copilot and AI agents on its fiscal Q4 2026 call. The stock has returned 34% in three months, against 2.5% for the S&P 500. Microsoft (MSFT) needs fast Azure growth and revenue from Copilot's paid seats to justify that gain. A year ago management led with a different topic, tied to a large part of Microsoft. What was it exactly.

items.title: Which Dates Could Move Microsoft Stock Most?
items.summary: Microsoft (MSFT) stock has gained about 34% in three months, and you may wonder whether it can hold that gain. Management expects about $175 billion of capital spending in calendar 2026 and has said the spending may lower operating margins. A few dated events will show whether that spending is paying off.
